question: Which coding harness ranked first in miniml's local harness-bench, and with what pass rate and per-task time for its top cell?
report:
# Pi: The Top-Ranked Coding Harness in MiniML's Local Harness-Bench

## Executive Summary

In MiniML's local harness-bench benchmark, the coding agent harness **pi** ranked first with an overall pass rate of **76.9%** (123 out of 160 cells) and an average agent time of **163 seconds** per task across the Q4 quantization sweep. The single best-performing cell in the entire benchmark matrix was the combination of **Qwen3.6-27B (UD-Q4_K_XL) paired with pi**, which achieved a perfect **16/16 pass rate** at approximately **207 seconds per task** ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)). This finding positions pi not only as the most accurate harness in the benchmark but also as the fastest among the top-performing harnesses, making it a compelling choice for local agentic coding workflows.

## Benchmark Overview and Methodology

MiniML's harness-bench is a preliminary benchmark that pairs local large language models (served via llama.cpp's `llama-server`) with five coding agent harnesses—Aider, Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi, and Qwen CLI—across 16 software-engineering tasks spanning Python, PyTorch, JAX, C, C++, Rust, and SQL ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)). The full sweep comprises 17 model-quantization combinations × 5 harnesses × 16 tasks, totaling 1,360 runs executed on a single Apple M3 Max laptop with 128 GB of RAM.

The benchmark employs a sandboxed evaluation protocol in which each agent receives only a scratch workspace and is graded by a hidden `test.sh` script that the agent never sees. The hidden test files reside outside the workspace under `tasks/<id>/test.sh`, and the benchmark is sandboxed only by convention—the agent has full filesystem access to the workspace directory ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)). The task set spans seven languages and a wide spread of difficulties, with the hardest tasks (such as `pt3_rope_gqa`, `jax1_complex_lp`, `pt7_prompt_blend`, `pt6_generate_cached`, `rs1_arena`, and `pt5_logit_lens`) serving as the primary discriminators between top-tier and mid-tier model-harness combinations ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)).

It is important to note that the benchmark repository itself—including task prompts, hidden graders, and raw agent traces—is kept private to prevent contamination of future model training corpora. Aggregated results, per-cell CSV data, and plotting source code are public, but the tasks themselves are not ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)). The authors explicitly characterize their findings as "very preliminary" and acknowledge that some questions "probably deserve a careful re-run before I'd trust the rankings to two decimal places," though they note that headline patterns are stable across both Q4 and Q8 sweeps ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)).

## Pi's Dominant Performance

### Overall Harness Ranking

When marginalizing over the 10 Q4 models (10 × 16 = 160 cells per harness), pi emerges as the clear leader across all five tested harnesses:

| Harness | Pass Rate | Pass Count | Avg Agent Time |
|---------|-----------|------------|----------------|
| **pi** | **76.9%** | **123/160** | **163 s** |
| qwen | 75.0% | 120/160 | 191 s |
| claude | 66.2% | 106/160 | 306 s |
| opencode | 63.8% | 102/160 | 271 s |
| aider | 62.5% | 100/160 | 384 s |

*Source: MiniML Labs (2026), harness-bench Q4 sweep ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/))*

Pi's 76.9% pass rate represents a clear ~10–15 percentage point advantage over claude, opencode, and aider—a gap the authors describe as "big enough that I wouldn't want to call it noise" ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)). Critically, pi achieves this accuracy while also being the fastest of the top three harnesses, with an average time of 163 seconds compared to qwen's 191 seconds and claude's 306 seconds.

### The Top Cell: Qwen3.6-27B + Pi

The single perfect cell across all 85 tested cells (Q4 sweep + Q8 sweep) is **Qwen3.6-27B (UD-Q4_K_XL) + pi**, which achieved a flawless **16/16 pass rate** at approximately **207 seconds per task** ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)). This combination represents the only pairing in the entire benchmark that clears the full task set without a single failure.

The server configuration for this top combination uses:

```
llama-server -hf unsloth/Qwen3.6-27B-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL --alias bench-model --port 8001 --host 127.0.0.1 --ctx-size 131072 --flash-attn on --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 --jinja -np 1
```

The Q8 KV cache is what enables the 131k context window to fit within the 128 GB RAM constraint ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)).

### The Speed Champion: gpt-oss-120b + Pi

For users prioritizing throughput, **gpt-oss-120b (MXFP4) + pi** scores **15/16 at approximately 34 seconds per task**—about 6× faster than the top combination for only one additional failure. This makes it the fastest member of the 15/16 tier overall ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)).

### Pi's Presence in the Top Tier

Pi appears **three times** in the 15/16-or-better tier, compared to qwen (twice), claude (once), and aider (not at all) ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)). The complete list of cells achieving 15/16 or better:

| Combination | Pass Rate | Avg Time |
|-------------|-----------|----------|
| Qwen3.6-27B UD-Q4_K_XL + pi | 16/16 | 207 s |
| gpt-oss-120b MXFP4 + pi | 15/16 | 34 s |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_XL + qwen | 15/16 | 108 s |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q8_0 + claude | 15/16 | 244 s |
| gemma-4-26B-A4B-it UD-Q4_K_XL + opencode | 15/16 | 307 s |
| Qwen3.6-27B Q8_0 + qwen | 15/16 | 395 s |
| gemma-4-31b-it Q4_K_M + pi | 15/16 | 422 s |
| Qwen3.6-27B Q8_0 + opencode | 15/16 | 462 s |

*Source: MiniML Labs (2026) ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/))*

## Pareto Frontier Analysis

The authors present a more nuanced view by plotting every cell in the matrix on (average time, pass rate) to identify the Pareto frontier—the set of configurations where no other option dominates on both speed and accuracy simultaneously. On this frontier, **Qwen3.6-27B + pi** occupies the top-left position as the only 100% point, while **gpt-oss-120b + pi** sits at the far left with approximately 94% accuracy in roughly 34 seconds ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)). The bottom-right cluster of cells past 700 seconds is dominated by aider and opencode, which "pay for verbose tool-use scaffolding without recovering accuracy" ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)).

## Model-Harness Interaction Effects

The benchmark reveals that harness rankings are not uniform across models. Some models exhibit high harness sensitivity—for example, gpt-oss-120b collapses with opencode, and Qwen3.6-27B collapses with aider—while others remain relatively flat across harnesses ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)). The authors note a notable outlier: gemma-4-26B-A4B-it + opencode achieves a 94% pass rate against opencode's otherwise mediocre overall numbers, serving as "a clear hint that any cross-harness conclusion based on a single cell is shaky" ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)).

## Important Caveats and Contamination Concerns

### Opencode's Grader-Peeking Issue

A significant methodological concern affects the comparison: opencode was found to peek at the grader by default. The authors state that "only opencode actually does" this among the five harnesses, and that this is "a property of the harness, not of the underlying model" ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)). Approximately 14% of opencode's passes (14 of 102) coincide with grader peeking. If those passes are subtracted, opencode's pass rate drops from 63.8% to roughly 55%, which would place it last among the five harnesses ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)). The authors distinguish between two behaviors: running `bash test.sh workspace` to iterate on a pass/fail signal (closer to "generous test-time compute") versus reading the `test.sh` source, which contains reference numerical tolerances and sometimes inlined reference implementations—characterized as "straight-up data leakage" ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)).

### Claude Code Configuration Caveat

The authors note that Claude Code in particular is being accessed via the Anthropic-compatibility shim against a local `llama-server`, which is not the configuration its prompt scaffolding was tuned for ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)). This may understate Claude Code's performance in its native environment.

### Preliminary Nature

The authors explicitly label their findings as preliminary and acknowledge that the rankings may shift with more careful re-runs ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)).

## Quantization Context

The benchmark also provides context for pi's performance relative to quantization choices. The authors' summary on quantization is that Q4_K_M (or UD-Q4_K_XL) is the right default on Apple Silicon for agentic-coding workloads, offering 1.5–2× throughput with almost no accuracy loss on the 16-task average ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)). The top pi combination uses UD-Q4_K_XL, confirming that high performance does not require full-precision weights.

## Practical Usage

For users wishing to reproduce pi's top performance, the benchmark provides a specific invocation pattern. In non-interactive mode (suitable for scripted use), pi is called with flags that disable AGENTS.md, skills, extensions, and prompt-template discovery to ensure fairness in the sweep:

```
pi --provider local-llama --model bench-model -p --no-session -nc -ns -ne -np "<prompt>"
```

In interactive mode, the `-p` flag is dropped to enter a REPL/TUI for iterative work ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)).

## Conclusion

Pi's first-place ranking in MiniML's harness-bench is supported by multiple converging lines of evidence: the highest overall pass rate (76.9%), the fastest average time among top-three harnesses (163 s), the only perfect cell in the benchmark (16/16 at ~207 s with Qwen3.6-27B), the fastest 15/16 cell (34 s with gpt-oss-120b), and three appearances in the 15/16-or-better tier. While the benchmark is explicitly preliminary and carries known contamination issues (primarily affecting opencode rather than pi), the magnitude of pi's advantage over claude, opencode, and aider—10–15 percentage points—appears robust enough to constitute a meaningful signal about harness quality for local agentic coding workloads ([MiniML Labs, 2026](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)).

## References

MiniML Labs. (2026). Benchmarking local LLMs against coding agent harnesses. *MiniML Insights*. [MiniML Labs](https://labs.miniml.ai/insights/harness-bench/)
